package_info.why_malicious: The provided report is a general discussion of software supply chain malware risks and detection strategies, not an analysis of a specific malicious package. It describes behavioral indicators and detection methodologies but does not reference or analyze any particular malicious package or code.

behavioral_signatures: Package released by an unfamiliar or new maintainer
Unusual release cadence (faster or slower than historical norm)
Significant change in the number of files in a package (increase or decrease)
Package name closely mimics a popular or trusted package (brandjacking/typosquatting)
Dependency confusion (package with same name as internal/private package)
file_indicators: Sudden addition or removal of files in a new version
Files with names similar to those in popular packages but with subtle differences
network_indicators: No specific domains or network behaviors mentioned in the report
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that deviate from their historical maintainer, release cadence, or file count. Flag packages with names similar to popular ones (brandjacking/typosquatting) or those that appear in public repositories with the same name as internal packages (dependency confusion). Use automated tools that analyze these behavioral signals and block suspicious packages before they enter the development environment.
